body: Sorry, yes, `v:progpath` should always point to the actual executable.
I will try to fix that

I found that the commit 24488169564c39a506c235bf6a33b8e23a8cb528 changed the behavior of `v:argv`.
Before that commit when running neovim from a symlink `./foo` : 
- `echo v:argv` would print `./foo`.

After that commit, the value of `v:argv` would contains the symlink target path (eg  : `['/tmp/neovim/build/bin/nvim', '--embed']`)

It is due to the fact that the function `ui_client_start_server` sets `argv[0]` to the value of `VV_PROGPATH`.
`VV_PROGPATH` contains the value of the target of the symlink (eg : instead of `./foo`, it will contains `/tmp/neovim/build/bin/nvim`).

```C
uint64_t ui_client_start_server(int argc, char **argv)
{
...
  args[args_idx++] = xstrdup((const char *)get_vim_var_str(VV_PROGPATH)); // Contains symlink target path
  args[args_idx++] = xstrdup("--embed");
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
    args[args_idx++] = xstrdup(argv[i]);
  }

  Channel *channel = channel_job_start(args, CALLBACK_READER_INIT,
                                       CALLBACK_READER_INIT, CALLBACK_NONE,
                                       false, true, true, false, kChannelStdinPipe,
                                       NULL, 0, 0, NULL, &exit_status);

```

I'm not sure what should be the behavior here ?  It should be easy to change `ui_client_start_server(int argc, char **argv)` that way to give correct argv[0] to ui process : 
```C

uint64_t ui_client_start_server(int argc, char **argv)
{
...
  args[args_idx++] = xstrdup((const char *)argv[0])); // Contains `./foo`
...
```

But for the `progpath` value, it seems that this variable has never worked the way expected in the issue.
I tried to compile `release-0.5` (older release did not compile on my laptop)  and `progpath` contained the target symlink path : 
- `echo v:progpath` -> `/tmp/neovim/build/bin/nvim`

This is because `VV_PROPATH` is set using `os_exepath` which is using `uv_exepath` from `libuv` that seems to follow the symlink. This should not be really hard to fix but I don't know if this the wanted behavior ?

I would appreciate some helps here.

Thanks
Using progpath to spawn the server process is fine. argv from the UI process have to be somehow sent to the server
ok, what would be the best way to send `argv` from the UI to the server ? is it with `rpc_send_event` ?

@t0muxx I think the best solution is to add a command line option that changes `argv[0]` and removes itself from `argv` when spawning the server. For example if you start with `nvim --embed-argv0 ./foo arg1 arg2`, `v:argv` should report `./foo arg1 arg2` + do what `--embed` does.

> I think the best solution is to add a command line option that changes `argv[0]` and removes itself from `argv` when spawning the server. For example if you start with `nvim --embed-argv0 ./foo `

Why do we need a new command line option? Can't the parent process call the child with the same arg0? Then the child only needs to remove `--embed` etc.
@justinmk Sure, that should work too. I assume then `--embed` would have to be unconditionally always removed from `v:argv`?

> I assume then `--embed` would have to be unconditionally always removed from `v:argv`?

The UI child knows it's a UI child, right? So let's start with that and see if it's good enough.
